topic: computing and interpreting center and spread
subtitle: Finding the mode, median and mean of a data set, measuring its spread with the range and the interquartile range, and deciding which of those numbers actually describes the group

traps.desc: averaged the six different goal totals on the axis instead of the eleven games
subtracted the smallest value from the largest, which is the range and not the interquartile range
counted the three goal totals of 3 or more on the axis instead of the games that reached them
reported the middle value of the ordered list, which is the median and not the mean

problems.desc: Open explanation, part (c). With Devi's 24 books in the set the mean is 8 and the median is 6; with her removed the mean drops to 6 and the median stays at 6. The student must argue which measure of centre describes this group of readers better and why, naming the effect of the single far-out value: the mean is computed from every value, so one reader far above the rest drags it upward until it sits higher than seven of the nine values, while the median only cares about position and barely moves. Accept any answer that identifies the outlier as the reason the two measures disagree AND commits to a measure with a reason (median, because it describes a typical reader; or mean, provided the student says the total matters here, e.g. for working out how many books the group read altogether). Do not accept an answer that only states the two numbers, or that says the mean is wrong without saying why one value can move it so far.

traps.desc: used the largest and smallest values, which gives the range rather than the interquartile range

problems.desc: Open explanation, part (c). The range of the summer-reading data is 21 and its interquartile range is 4.5. The student must explain why the interquartile range gives a fairer picture of how spread out this group is: the range is computed from exactly two values and here one of them is the single far-out reader, so it describes the gap to that one student rather than the group; the interquartile range measures the width of the middle half, which the far-out value cannot move. Accept any answer that says the range depends on only the two extreme values (or explicitly on the outlier) while the interquartile range describes the middle half of the data. Do not accept an answer that only says 4.5 is smaller than 21, or that the interquartile range is better without saying what each one measures.
